acceptance: Decision gate: no new make target unless the owner wants one; do not add bytes to the six budgeted instruction files.
Verification: `make help | grep -i 'local review'` shows the pr-open line saying it runs the review; a docs/agent page gives the standalone command; make docs-validate passes.
description:
Found on 2026-11-11 while delivering retro-navigation-fixes-umbrella-20261111 (or in the retrospective over 25 agent sessions that preceded it) and not addressed there.

Problem. `make pr-open` runs the local review (`scripts/local_review.py`), but no make target name, AGENTS.md line or docs/agent page says so; it is described only in docs/internal/review-v2.md under 'Local pre-PR review'. In one reviewed session an agent searched the make targets, concluded no local review existed, and ran another CLI as a reviewer six times until the owner objected. An AGENTS.md sentence was considered and does not fit the 17,300-byte instruction budget (17,269 used).

Change. State it where agents already look without spending instruction bytes: the `make pr-open` help line and docs/agent/merge-authority.md or docs/agent/preflight-receipt.md, with the command to run the review alone before pushing.

Guardrails: work in a linked worktree (make worktree-create, then make agent-write-preflight); never edit the primary clone, and pass absolute worktree paths to every file tool; stage paths explicitly; no explanatory comments or docstrings (make comment-policy-check); heavy work only via make heavy-run, never forcing admission; never bypass a required check, ruleset, hold label or review gate; re-read every cited file on current origin/develop first, because line numbers and commits here are from 2026-11-11 (origin/develop 5bd2c19cc4); close at a merged PR and finish only after the merge is observed.
